description: OpenTripPlanner for R is an R interface to the OpenTripPlanner routing service. It can start and manage a local OpenTripPlanner instance, connect to an existing remote server, send routing requests and bring the results back into R. The documentation also covers batch routing and isochrones. The software works on a transport network supplied to the underlying service, so its spatial coverage and analysis period depend on the GTFS, street and service data used for that instance. The R package source and usage guides are public under GPL-3.0. It can help measure access to facilities, compare travel times after a transit disruption, or prepare routes for a transport simulation. It is a client and setup layer; it does not replace the Java routing engine or provide a current transport feed. Server availability and the quality of timetable and street data affect results, and large requests can depend on server capacity. The related catalogue record model-opentripplanner describes the underlying routing engine. This review checked the JOSS description, repository and README, but did not install the R package or operate a server.
